title: CYBRIK server-neutral transport peer evidence v1
description: Server-neutral description of what a relying party learned about its transport peer from the serving side of a mutually-authenticated TLS connection, and nothing else. This document is EVIDENCE, never AUTHORIZATION: it carries no token, no scope, no approval and no capability, and `conveys_authorization` is structurally pinned to false. Raw certificate material is structurally inexpressible — no PEM, no DER, no public key, no subject, no subject alternative name, and no caller- or header-asserted thumbprint has anywhere to live. The only admissible peer identifier is the RFC 8705 3.1 'x5t#S256' thumbprint, and it is REUSED by $ref from the ACCEPTED W2-F cybrik.svc-common-defs.v1 certThumbprint definition rather than restated here. $id uses the RFC 2606 reserved .example documentation domain; it is a stable identifier, NOT an operational endpoint. Status: ACCEPTED FOR IMPLEMENTATION — NOT IMPLEMENTED, v0.1.0; not stable v1/GA and not a bundle tag. Gate W2-K, ADR-0013.

conveys_authorization.description: Pinned false. Peer evidence never authorizes an operation; authorization stays in the ACCEPTED W2-F delegation-token layer.

channelEvidence.description: What the serving side observed on the transport channel. `additionalProperties` is false so certificate material and header-asserted identity are structurally inexpressible, not merely discouraged.

evidence_state.description: `present` only when the serving side actually supplied channel evidence. `absent` and `held` both fail closed; neither may degrade to an unauthenticated accept.

mutual_tls.description: True only when the peer presented a client certificate on a mutually-authenticated TLS connection.

chain_verified.description: True only when the serving side verified the peer chain against its configured trust anchors. An unverified chain is never upgraded by any later step.

peerThumbprint.description: The RFC 8705 3.1 certificate thumbprint of the transport peer. `alg` is pinned to x5t#S256, so a SHA-1 shaped or otherwise weaker thumbprint is structurally inexpressible. `value` REUSES the ACCEPTED W2-F certThumbprint definition by $ref and is deliberately not restated here.

peerThumbprintSource.description: Where the thumbprint came from. Only serving-side sources are expressible; a client-supplied, header, proxy-asserted or forwarded-client-cert source has no enumerated value and can never be stated.

relyingPartyObservation.description: The thumbprint the relying party independently derived for the same peer. Its presence is what makes the three-way equality checkable; its absence is a denial, never an implicit match.

tokenConfirmation.description: The RFC 8705 confirmation method of the presented delegation token, REUSED by $ref from the ACCEPTED W2-F cnfConfirmation definition. This document restates neither the confirmation shape nor the thumbprint pattern.

serverNeutrality.description: The packet selects no server. `selected_server` is pinned to null and `adapter_profile` admits exactly the server-verified-chain adapter, so the forbidden trusted-boundary shortcut cannot be expressed by any conforming document.

adapterProfile.description: The only admissible adapter profile. A trusted-boundary adapter — one that would accept a peer identity asserted by an upstream hop instead of one verified by the serving side — is named only as forbidden and is inexpressible here.
